reviews.author: Jennie B.
reviews.comment: This was great. It was easy to use on my older Sony and you’ll have more shows and movies than you could ever watch in a lifetime. Good value for the money. I like it better than my smart tv for sure. Faster than the smart tv too.

reviews.author: Alan Whitt
reviews.comment: The Firestick works well and it comes with the USB cable to power it. It DOES NOT have the HDMI extender cable packaged with it, but they do offer one in the instruction info that you can order. I didn't want to wait so I picked up a pack of 90-degree adapters from Walmart. The Firestick is about 4" long and needs 'straight-in' access to your HDMI port. You will have to link it to your Amazon account.The remote functions are simple to use once you get used to it. The home screen reminds me of a cable TV screen -modernized. There are a lot of channel options (I haven't tried any),but I just punch the Netflix button. Picture and sound quality is better than what I had.I'm liking it so far!

reviews.author: Maynard*Is*My*God
reviews.comment: ******RETURN UPDATE******They offered to let me keep this stupid thing while giving me a partial refund of $4. They are basically trying to pay people to keep them ROFLMAOAmazon, y'all just made my point for me. Thanks, but no thanks.******UPDATE******The more I poke around in the settings the less I like this thing, and I don't think I've even had it a full week. I can't enable the developer options without creating a developer account. I don't need or want a developer account. I want to enable installations from unknown sources, and that particular option used to be in the now inaccessible developer options. I see now that the installation of apps from unknown sources is not allowed, for "enhanced security." It would have been lovely to have seen that little message before I bought this crap, because I wouldn't have bothered buying it. Amazon, how about you let ME worry about the security of MY device? You know, the device you sent me after you took my money for it? That means I own it, and I get to do whatever I wish with it. Including installing whatever app I want regardless of the source. I don't appreciate having the option for installing apps from unknown sources removed in the name of "security" when it's likely just because someone at Amazon can't handle the thought of people putting apps that Amazon has pretty much no authority over on THE DEVICE THAT THEY PAID FOR. Amazon, you most certainly DO NOT GET TO DICTATE WHAT I INSTALL ON MY DEVICES. And that ridiculous "we cannot detect your remote" message needs to disappear from all fire sticks (both old and new) forever. Apparently the gods have forbidden turning on the TV without immediately pressing buttons on the remote. Y'all seem to think that just because I don't immediately start scrolling through all the uninteresting garbage on the home page as soon as it loads that "something must be wrong with the device!" There's nothing wrong with my remote; it's not too far from the stick that's in the TV, and the batteries are just fine. Stop harrassing people via their TV screens. Newer does NOT mean better. I think I'm going to send this one back and just get a new cable for my old one, which is probably what I should have done in the first place since it still works just fine even though it's 6 or 7 years old. Or better yet, I'll send this trash device back and get a new Roku. I'm just glad my first fire stick was a gift. I do believe I'm finished with the Amazon brand for anything. Amazon.com has grossly overestimated its own importance in the lives of the general populace.I just got this thing today, and I can't really say I'm a fan so far. I'm currently going through all the apps that Amazon so graciously installed on my device (without first asking if I wanted them) and removing them. Why do you assume everyone has netflix? Why do you assume I want all this crap on my device? If I want an app then I know how to search for and download it myself. Channels, News, Sports, En Español, Kids+, Youtube, etc. I don't need or want any of this crap. And the screensaver settings are nonexistent. I want to disable it, but I cannot. And heaven forbid I pause something and go outside to have a cigarette. It'll reset itself to the home screen within 10 minutes (or is it a whole five minutes?), and then I have to go back to the app I was using and find what I was watching so that I can continue watching whatever it might have been. And where did my apps on the home screen go? I'm already getting sick of having to use the search function to find apps that were right at the top of my home screen on my old fire stick. I honestly don't know that I even want to keep this infuriating little piece of trash, because I've done nothing but ask myself why I spent perfectly good money on it since I finished the setup.And just to be clear, I really liked the one I just replaced. My only gripe with the old one was the lack of screensaver settings. I WANT TO DISABLE THE STUPID SCREENSAVER.

reviews.author: blondie54
reviews.comment: GREAT device....quick to set-up and use. Pretty initiative to use and add apps. However, just an FYI: for those that do not have an available USB port on their tv....or it is not rated high enough for the 2026 HD fire stick - and want to re-use the regular wall power adapter and standard micro USB cable that came with another fire stick...THEY ARE NOT COMPATIBLE. The micro connection port on the new 2026 HD Fire Stick is a USB C type of connection (looks like a small oval) and the connection on the end of the wall adapter cable is a standard micro, so will not fit. So IF you are needing to use the wall power adapter, you might have to buy a new USB -C cable to connect.... if your electric outlet is more than a foot away from the fire stick, which mine was. Other than that the new 2026 HD fire stick works great.

reviews.author: Therese Shellabarger
reviews.comment: Perfect for the HD user, even works without a TV, as long as you have HDMI connectivity. You will need to provide your own power adapter if your device of choice doesn't have a spare USB port for power. FYI, the manual states that you need a 5 Watt power adapter. I used the one that Amazon sent with my (nonworking) 4K Fire Stick and it was fine. Setup was very quick and you just need your WiFi password which you can use either the Amazon Fire app for Android or Apple to speed things up, or stick to using the remote. Picture quality was great and sound was clear. I also set up closed captions as that's something I use all the time, very easy to do. I think the remote takes some getting used to, but it's OK. Amazon doesn't seem to have as many of the free apps as Roku does, but maybe I just have to explore the Amazon appstore more.

reviews.author: joseph D Pergolotti
reviews.comment: The Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Select has been working great and is a noticeable upgrade from older streaming devices. Setup was quick and straightforward, and once connected to Wi-Fi, I was up and streaming in just a few minutes.The picture quality is excellent, and apps open quickly without much waiting. The interface is easy to navigate, and having all my favorite streaming services in one place makes watching TV much more convenient.The remote is simple to use, and I really like the voice-control feature for finding shows and movies without having to type everything out.Overall, this is a fast, compact streaming device that delivers great picture quality without taking up any space. A very good value and an easy way to upgrade an older TV.

reviews.author: T Trigo
reviews.comment: I am incredibly impressed. I say again, I am incredibly impressed! Tech stuff often doesn't work as well or as easily as it should. I replaced an older Fire Stick with this device and for not much more than $20, let me say again - I am incredibly impressed! I decided to play around with the "equipment" control features. I had been using a Logitech Harmony universal remote which had become somewhat unreliable after years' of service. I never expected this to control not only my tv, but my AV receiver as well. It did, and the setup was remarkably easy. I'm pretty much an Apple guy, but this was for a setup in my kitchen so I wasn't ready to spend for an Apple TV. I was blown away with how easy this was and how well it works. Kudos to the Amazon engineers/developers! Apple products should be so intuitive!

reviews.author: larry d
reviews.comment: Terrible. It wont stay paired to my TV and I have tried everything. Was my first review? Since then I have had numerous people from Amazon reach out to me to offer help. They were able to walk me through the fix. So one star becomes four.

reviews.author: Randy Foster
reviews.comment: Xfinity Stream App heads up... Some users have posted reviews that this model does not work with the Xfinity Stream App. When I was setting up my Fire TV Stick 4K Select, it would not let me download the Xfinity Stream App as other users have noted in their reviews. The Amazon App Store kept saying that my Fire Stick didn't have the correct OS and needed an update. Ok, I went to the settings and told it to look for and update the OS. It kept repeatedly saying it was up to date and no update available. This was annoying as I bought these to replace Xfinity cable boxes to save on those monthly box rental costs (on older smart TV's that can't run Xfinity Stream natively). After some internet searches, I found the solution. When you buy these Firesticks, they are already registered to your Amazon account when they ship to you. The solution to getting these units to have the correct firmware and setup is to unregister the Fire Stick from your Amazon account and then re-register it. Its ridiculously easy. It rebuilds the setup and OS in the process. Now when you go to the App Store to download the Xfinity Stream App, everything works the way it should. Very happy with how these work with Xfinity Stream on my TVs.

reviews.author: Dan Miner
reviews.comment: Hmm...well, I purchased a new one from Amazon yet it showed up all taped up and stuff. Everything was there, I mean, it was just quite evident the device I received was not new. New to me, is that it? Jokes on me? I'm just joshing. A little passive-aggression before bed ought to help me sleep.haSo this one plugs in like all the others. It works the same as all the others. Having Alexa Plus on the remote is handy. Some nights the TV just sits on Amazon Fire home screen and Alexa and I dive into quantum mechanics, physics, every kind of science imaginable and don't get her started on the Universe! That's the one that "really lights up my circuits"-end quote.lol But yeah, the microphone remote is awesome to have for sure.Man these remotes...they're super thin and don't have much to them and I am constantly looking for mine. I have a 4k Max Firestick in my living room...same d@mn problem. In the couch, under the couch, under the coffee table's bottom shelf and a whole LOT of the time...under the cat.haha My point, now that I thought of one, is it'd be killer to have it like the Roku Ultra remote, man. The Roku has a "find remote button" on it and the remote starts beeping and stays on long enough to find it too. Just that would be sweet, but Roku took it one more step and put that ⅛" headphone jack on it. That is...just...no words so nice. It beats batteries DOWN. Hard. And fast...like, 3 hours at high volume. But, eh...fair trade.Wait, I should be writing this in a suggestion box I think, not a review. Is that a thing? Amazon taking suggestions?The settings are easy to...set. It's plug-and-play ready to go out of the box with passwords and stuff already programmed. Nice to alleviate that migraine...and somehow it links right up to wifi even tho they don't know the password...all my Amazon stuff does that.I have all the different streaming gizmos. I like to call them the "Eternity Stones of Streaming". Roku and Chromecast, Xumo, etc etc But I definitely, 100% use the firesticks way more than the rest. Combined even. For sure. Just easiest and fastest.Oh, and this one does Xbox like the Max. I'm telling you a week or so after I got a firestick device that let me use Xbox live and actually play games I sold my Xbox console, kept 2 wireless controllers and game on this thing. It's the same. And , the Xbox controller doubles as a regular firestick remote as well. Yes, I learned that because I am always loosing this slippy lil firestick remote.Does everyone know you can expand the memory on the firesticks? I use an OTG cable and then either a flash drive or SD card. You can hold too many apps if you wanted. You can download your latest bootleg 'still in theaters' movie from Limewire onto a flash drive, take it to a friend's place and pop it in the firestick. BOOM. There it is. Showing up with the new movies!I dont know if these do the Amazon Sidewalk thing like echo devices, and then again I don't know anyone that bothers to turn it off. But, in case you're that person and I just don't know you, I'd check to see.

name: Apple EarPods Headphones with USB-C Plug, Wired Ear Buds with Built-in Remote to Control Music, Phone Calls, and Volume

reviews.author: Tiffany Wright
reviews.comment: The Apple EarPods with USB-C Plug are a great choice for anyone who wants the simplicity, reliability, and sound quality of classic wired earbuds without worrying about charging or battery life. They’re a convenient everyday option for music, phone calls, podcasts, and video.The USB-C connection makes these EarPods compatible with newer Apple devices that no longer use a traditional headphone jack, providing a simple plug-and-play experience. There’s no pairing process, no Bluetooth connection issues, and no need to remember to charge them before use.The built-in remote and microphone are incredibly convenient for everyday use. With easy controls for adjusting volume, playing or pausing music, skipping tracks, and answering calls, everything is accessible right from the cord. The microphone also provides clear call quality for conversations on the go.The iconic EarPods design is comfortable for many users because it sits naturally in the ear without the pressure of silicone tips. They’re lightweight, making them great for extended listening sessions at work, while traveling, exercising, or relaxing at home.The sound quality is impressive for a compact wired earbud, delivering clear vocals, balanced audio, and reliable performance for everyday listening. They’re also a great backup pair to keep in a bag, car, or desk drawer.Overall, Apple EarPods with USB-C Plug are a practical, dependable, and affordable audio accessory. They offer the convenience of wired listening, excellent compatibility, and the familiar Apple quality many users appreciate. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.author: BalkShiba
reviews.comment: Very solid pair of headphones with Apple quality. The material is about the same as the previous iterations, and the usbc cable is great for almost all devices that I used this with. Although it might not be suitable for exercise, it makes up for it in being versatile and has no compatibility isssues with any of the devices that I used it with. If I have an important meeting that I have to attend, these are my go to pair. These earphones offer insane value for the money and have no connectivity issues as of yet. These are not noise cancelling, but the design makes the audio crisp and not muffled at all

reviews.author: sofia
reviews.comment: These are always the best EarPods, even my husband prefers them and he uses an android phone! Great sound, strong material, not bulky. Comfortable. I never hsby tech issues with them. Sound and mic are great quality and clarity

reviews.author: Amazon Customer
reviews.comment: Great quality, durability, connection and value for my money. They work well for zoom & MyChart calls. The sound is clear and dependable. They are great for privacy. They also work well for the elderly who don’t use hearing aids but need help hearing phone calls, music and MyChart video calls.

reviews.author: Markdett
reviews.comment: The Best EarPods for me! I hate Bluetooth earbuds because they never seem to position correctly in my ears, for good sound. I had a pair of the Apple AirPods too, but they were so comfortable I forgot the were in and I’d lose them and didn’t even know they fell out. Don’t get me wrong, they’re great too, but way more expensive but I’ve jumped in the shower with them on, been up in an attic and one fell out into the insulation and if you know about insulation, there was no chance of finding it. I was tired of paying $300. This is the 2nd set of wired apple earbuds I’ve bought in a few months. Not because they’re not good buds, but because I lost the first set, or so I thought. I ordered the 2nd set after a few days of looking, but then as I was unloading clothes from the washer , to place in the dryer, I found them wrapped around other clothes. And now I have 2 functional sets because washing them did not damage them in the least. They still play well in both ears and the controls still work. Now I have a backup pair. I think imma stick with these $20 buds

shortDescription: Apple AirPods Pro 3 Wireless Earbuds with Active Noise Cancellation
fullDescription: Apple AirPods Pro 3 Wireless Earbuds with Active Noise Cancellation

reviews.author: Dean Ehrenheim
reviews.comment: Fit and sound are perfect.I had a free pair of airpods from an old phone. I could never get them to stay in my ear and there was NO noise cancelling. I decided to try this new version hoping the fit was improved. Also, I feel like I am getting a bit of hearing loss and the fact they could adapt for minor hearing loss was a big plus.So glad I got them. The sound fills your head. And the noise cancelling is nothing short of amazing. I took the Airpod hearing test and was told I had little hearing loss, so I have not set them up as an adi to my hearing...but still could.The only problem I have had is from time to time one of the ear pods won't charge. It seems that re-seating them has helped. These are worth the extra I invested from cheaper earpods. I am a convert.

reviews.author: Alex Rogers
reviews.comment: I have a set of Airpods pro, 1st gen, that have served me well for a good few years now.They were great for travel and for work, but not so good for sports. I also have a pair of Beats fit Pro which I use for workouts and for reading at night. These were almost as good in terms of sound quality, but much better than the original Airpods Pro in terms of battery duration and comfort and staying power for intense workouts.Lately, however, the battery of my old Airpods hardly lasts through a couple of work meetings, so it was clearly time to renew, and I decided to take advantage of a price drop on the Pro 3.I expected improvement, but I wasn't ready for how much vastly better than the original Pros these are!They're far more comfortable and hang far more tenaciously than the original pros, so they work well for workouts as well.But the sound quality is an enormous leap, and mind you, the original pros weren't bad at all!The noise cancellation is ... amazing. The way in which practically every noise just disappears, and you're fully immersed only into what's coming through the earphones was truly disconcerting at first.And I have no idea how this works, but without noise cancellation, it somehow manages to convey with greater clarity and sharpness, not only what other people say to me, but also what I say as well. It's like getting a good pair of glasses when you didn't realize you were somewhat myopic.I am far less sold on the instant translation feature, though.So far I have only been able to test it with a TV show, and the results have been less than great.The translation tends to get cut off a lot - I think you need to be very close to a real human speaker, or have the volume rather loud, for the microphone to pick sound well enough for the AI to translate.And the choice of words is not always accurate. I heard some very weird things that the speaker could not possibly be saying in the context given - plus I know enough French to know that some if it was just plain wrong.I assume that will improve with time.Othewise, I am delighted with my new Airpods.

reviews.author: Jeremiah kross
reviews.comment: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Amazon Review: Apple AirPods Pro 3 Wireless Earbuds with Active Noise CancellationThese earbuds exceeded my expectations in both sound quality and comfort. The audio is crisp and well-balanced, with deep bass, clear vocals, and excellent detail across all types of music and podcasts. The Active Noise Cancellation does an outstanding job of blocking out background noise, making it easy to focus whether I’m traveling, working, or exercising.The earbuds fit securely and comfortably for extended listening sessions, and the multiple ear tip sizes make it easy to find the right fit. Pairing with Apple devices is seamless, and switching between my iPhone, iPad, and Mac is quick and effortless.Call quality is excellent, with voices coming through clearly even in noisier environments. The transparency mode is another standout feature, allowing me to stay aware of my surroundings without removing the earbuds.Overall, these earbuds deliver premium sound, exceptional comfort, and the convenience you’d expect from Apple’s ecosystem. If you’re looking for high-quality wireless earbuds with excellent noise cancellation and reliable everyday performance, these are an outstanding choice and well worth considering.

reviews.author: Michael Federer
reviews.comment: These are amazing, and it almost feels like I am in a Black Mirror episode with how futuristic these are. First of all the sound quality is fine, I feel like it does great for in ear headphones, but I would say it doesn't blow me away like some IEM's I have used. The connectivity is amazing, and with all my Apple products it makes this more than worth it for people that have a bunch of Apple products, and it will switch between my MacBook Air and iPhone seamlessly without having to manually switch. The noise cancelling is the thing that blew my mind. I put them in, turned on the noise cancelling and listened to music. I then blasted a video through my speakers, and although the table was shaking because it was so loud, I couldn't hear it. Almost dangerously good, and if there were no way to turn off noise cancelling I probably wouldn't recommend them because of lack of situational awareness. On that note, the transparent mode is really good, and sometimes I will wear these and listen to music in transparent mode, and it's almost like there is a background track in your life. I like that there is a bunch of rubber tip size options that come with it, and there is a setting that lets you test the noise leak to see if the ear tips are the right size. The live translate was one of the reasons that I bought it. I have some in-laws that do not speak English, so I thought it would be a great feature to converse with them. I used these to translate Brazilian Portuguese to English, and it worked well, but it needed a small break after the person was done speaking to read it back to me. I don't know why but I feel like with the noise cancellation they could have it so that it would translate while the person was still talking, but it really worked best when the person would say a sentence or two and give a brief pause to let it read it back to me. It also worked better when I was speaking English and translating it to BR Portuguese for my fiancé, and the translation seemed to be pretty immediate. I bet this will get better as it is still in Beta. I also really like the potential they have as hearing aids, as I am hard of hearing, and I could see myself using these for audio amplification. I had regular Airpod 2's and these blow those away. The main reason that I made the switch is actually because of the charigng ability. I hated that my old ones were still charged by lightning and couldn't wirelessly charge. These are USB-C and charge wirelessly, and so now I only have to bring my Belkin 3 in 1 wireless charge when I travel, and I can charge my iPhone, Apple Watch Ultra, and new air pods with only one cord. Overall I would and recommend these to anybody and everybody that enjoys in ear headphones, and I have shown them off to a bunch of friends and family who bought them immediately.

reviews.author: Cory Harris
reviews.comment: Coming from using the AirPod pro V1 and finally upgrading to the V3 after all these years is fantastic. The sound quality is clear and the new intuitive gestures are a nice feature. The bass isn’t as strong as my beats pros that I had, and then subsequently lost, but they are punchy none the less. Noise cancelling is fantastic but I find myself using the adaptive mode so I can still hear what going on around me while still blocking out loud noises. Catch these while they are still on sale.PS they are also compatible with Nintendo switch/switch 2 consoles which is a huge plus for me.

reviews.author: Kimberly
reviews.comment: This was my first air tag. I bought it for my suitcase. It worked exactly as I expected.The packaging was compact, well protected, and easy to open. The air tag arrived in perfect condition with the battery already installed. Setup with my iPhone took less than a minute. It appeared automatically and connected without any issues. The Find My app made it simple to name the AirTag.The location updates have been accurate. The precision finding feature is especially helpful. The sound is clear enough to hear from another room. The airtag is small, lightweight, and easy to attach to a key ring or slip into a backpack or suitcase. The battery compartment is secure, and the quality is excellent. Everything has worked reliably so far. If you already use Apple devices, this is an easy way to keep track of important items. I’m very happy with it. Good value for the money. I thought AirTags were more expensive!

reviews.author: Jbeard
reviews.comment: I purchased the 4-pack of Apple AirTags specifically for my dogs, and they've given me so much peace of mind. They were incredibly easy to set up, connected to my iPhone within minutes, and work seamlessly with the Find My app.The tracking is accurate and reliable, making it easy to quickly locate my dogs if they wander around the yard or when we're out and about. The compact size is perfect for attaching to their collars, and they don't seem to notice they're wearing them.The battery life is excellent, and I appreciate the precision finding feature when one of the tags ends up tucked under a blanket or in another room. Buying the 4-pack was also a great value since I could outfit all of my dogs at once.If you're looking for a dependable way to keep track of your pets, these AirTags are an excellent investment. They provide extra peace of mind, are incredibly easy to use, and I highly recommend them to any pet owner.

reviews.author: LJ
reviews.comment: I bought the 4-pack for an upcoming trip. I also occasionally misplace my keys, so this will reduce frustration and time spent searching for them. They’re pricey, but that’s typical for all Apple products, and I’ve found them to be worth it. The packaging is outstanding, protects them from damage, and it’s easy to open. Setup was quick and simple. Have your iPhone nearby. Just pull the tab holding the paper covering on each airtag, and your phone will prompt you. There are categories already set up so you can label each one, i.e., keys, luggage, backpack, etc. as you activate it, and it automatically ties it to your location. There’s an option to turn off notifications for when each airtag is located at your home address. Although not required, I highly recommend purchasing AirTag holders. The AirTags are by design small and portable, and they’re also round and slick, so it’s easy to lose them if they’re not physically connected to whatever you’re trying to protect and locate if lost or misplaced. A set of 4 of the silicone ones popped up for purchase when I put the 4 pack of AirTags in my shopping cart. They help protect the AirTag, but most importantly, they allow you to securely connect the AirTag to your keys, luggage, or whatever. The ones I bought are in 4 different colors, so it’s easy for me to identify which one is which. I just got the AirTags, so I can’t say yet how reliable or accurate they are, but I’ll update this review if there are any issues.

That way when he needs his remote or if he can’t find it, all he has to do grab the yarn tied to the headboard and fish it out from wherever it’s hiding. He loves that. He said it has simplified something that used to drive him crazy, lol.Finally I was able to get myv90 year old father to get rid of cable tv where he was paying$140/per month just for the cable tv basic too 120 channels plus two Filipino channels charged at $10 each ($20 total) per month. reviews.author: Bubba Pearson
reviews.comment: This is a fairly good headset with decent sound that does an adequate job at music reproduction. They are fairly inexpensive, so going with the old accepted 'wisdom' that you get what you pay for, I really hadn't expected much from them when I made the purchase, so they've pretty much lived up to that lofty expectation. Anyway, I've used them pretty much on a daily basis for months now without really given them much thought, so I've been happy enough. After all, they were affordable. They aren't particularly uncomfortable. They didn't sound horrible and they seem to be all I need for the use to which I put them. I unplugged the old set, put 'em away, plugged in these and that was that. Because I wasn't expecting much, I never considered doing any sort of quality testing or comparison listening when they arrived. That was a mistake. With clear hindsight, I'd now say I'd already pretty much convinced myself they would do when I ordered them, so I never bothered to check if they actually were. Naturally they sound okay, since I wasn't expecting much, but they're being used almost exclusively for non-critical, background listening to music on my tablet while I'm doing other things (almost anything instead of watching the idiot box while my wife is in the same room, online and talking with her coworkers and clients and trying to concentrate on her new full-time, off-site job). So, since I haven't really been thinking about anything more than whether or not they reproduce music, they're okay. Not awful, not great, but okay. That's what I expected so that's pretty much what I got. I should have been more careful.A couple of days ago my wife was out exercising before starting her work shift, so I took advantage of the opportunity to test-drive some new music I was thinking about purchasing. I needed to be more discerning in my listening and I needed to be online, so I moved over to my desk so I could use my souped-up PC and Klipsch Promedia 2.1 speaker system, a combination that reproduces music pretty well for me. I realized from the outset I couldn't expect to favorably compare my inexpensive Sony 'phones to that, but I was completely surprised even so. I'd never checked, so I never realized just how much of the music I'd been missing with the new headphones.Now I started thinking about my headphones a bit more critically, the old and new. Yes, the old set was a bit long in the tooth; after all, it was quite a few years old and had seen a lot of use. Even so, I'd replaced it not because of a problem with the sound reproduction, but because the connector cable was wearing out and getting a bit ratty. Worse, it had developed a somewhat quirky connector that often required reseating in the jack to work. A pain in the butt, but when they worked, they still sounded quite good. I then remembered listening to music and thinking about just how great it sounded on a brand new laptop I used recently (with the old headset). At the time, I attributed the great sound pretty much entirely to the new sound chip in the costly new Dell, but maybe it had been more than just the laptop.Time and past time for action! I pulled open the junk drawer in my desk and started digging around, movin' aside all the old serial cables, card readers, cabled mouses (mice?) and such until I found the cloth bag I'd stored my old headphones in when I got the new set. I disconnected the Sony's, set 'em aside and plugged in the old ones. Rats: same old problem. I reach up and jiggle the connector around this way and that, push it in a bit further and pull it out a skosh until it's just right and finally, sound! Wow. I noticed immediately that the music was much more detailed than it had been with the new headphones. I was clearly hearing vocals and instruments as distinct individual elements, instead of, or rather, in addition to the one musical whole produced by the entire band I heard with the Sony headphones. A very noticeable difference. So I listened carefully for awhile, unplugged the old set and tried the newer Sony set again for a couple of songs, then unplugged them again and reconnected the old headphones. There was absolutely no doubt about it -- the old no-name headset (only about $20 more expensive than the new Sony's) absolutely reproduced the music with more clarity and even a deeper low end.Now what to do? Well, when I'm not paying close attention to the music, the Sony headphones and my Samsung tablet are fine, so I have those in the living room beside my easy chair (to use while my wife is working). If I want better sound while she's at work, now I have the option to move over to my desk and use my old headphones on my desktop. Not ideal maybe, but it works for me. I still have the problem with the connector on the old set every now and again, but unless and until it breaks down completely, it works.Bottom line? These inexpensive Sony headphones work, they're not uncomfortable, they're not even close to being awful, so they may be perfect for listening to music in the background or other such offhand use where not too much attention will be paid to the details. Folks that aren't too picky about music or really don't care about all the subtle little nuances that better, more expensive headphones reproduce accurately should be happy with this inexpensive choice. Again, they're not awful, they're not great, but they are okay. On the other hand, for some being merely okay really might not be all that okay, so if that's you, or music in all its multifaceted, heavily nuanced glory is more your thing, it might be better to think about something better.

reviews.author: Manda Rae
reviews.comment: I'd resisted the wireless headphone trend for as long as possible, preferring the regular 3.5mm jack. Unfortunately, iPhone thought it would be a good idea to get rid of the headphone jack altogether. I disagree with this decision, but I don't make phones, so... I used regular wired headphones with a connector thingy to be able to plug it into my phone for a while. That worked fine, except for the fact that the connectors would inevitably stop working after a while. So I went through many of those. Then one day, my phone stopped working with connectors. No matter what I did, the volume would go back to zero and I couldn't use the headphones at all. So finally I decided to get wireless headphones, even though I once heard it's like the equivalent of putting a microwave in each of your ears. Oh well, it's 2026 and wifi and 5G and whatever else is all over the place. But then I had to go down the rabbit hole of finding headphones that were worth it. I didn't want super expensive or fancy wireless headphones for listening to music with my phone. I have over-ear Sony headphones that I use for recording and sound editing, I just really needed something to listen to music on my phone with while going for a walk. Reading reviews was frustrating and took me all over the place. Finally I decided to go with my gut and just order these. They're fine. I'm a bit of a sound snob and I need bass. These are fine. They fit well enough and comfortable enough in my ears. They don't get as loud as I would prefer, but that's probably a good thing. The bass is decent. The overall sound feels balanced for the most part. They hold a charge for a long time, too. I've only charged the case once since I bought them a couple months ago and I don't even know if they were close to needing a charge. I only really use them when I go for a walk around the neighborhood. I use them to listen to music and have not tried to use them for a call or anything. They seem easy to use, though admittedly I don't care to be bothered to learn what all the various tap combinations do. I put them in my ears, they automatically pair with my phone after the initial pairing, and I use the controls on my phone for volume and track changes. This works for me. They are fine. I do not think ANY wireless headphones have the sound quality of wired headphones, so these are fine. The sound is fine. I'm not like, "oh wow! these are amazing!" but I am happily listening to tunes as the soundtrack to my walks. I like how they fit in the case and its easy enough to throw them in my purse. I almost dropped one once, and I did not like that feeling of not being able to catch them with a cord but, that's me. I will say it is nice not to have to deal with the cord in terms of it being in the way while walking around or getting tangled in a purse. I have no idea about the water resistance because that's not something I deal with while wearing headphones. In terms of noise cancellation... it's not something I've really noticed, but now that I think about it I don't really notice the sound of the traffic/cars on the street while I am walking. This may or may not be a good thing. But I am happy with them. For the price, I am happy with them. For the sound, I am happy with them. For the purpose of walking while listening to music, I am happy with them. If you are also going down the rabbit hole of reviews trying to find basic earbuds for music listening purposes, I do suggest getting these and saving yourself any more frustration. They're not perfect, they're not incredible, but they are just fine.

In terms of performance, they completely exceeded my expectations. reviews.author: thirst4music
reviews.comment: Sometimes I'm amazed by the advancements in wireless and micro technology, especially when it comes to audio. These popped up in an email from Amazon a few days ago. Though I usually ignore those Deal notices this one intrigued me. I have a JBL Everest over-ear headset that I love for indoor phone calls and they're pretty good for music too (though I don't use them that way). I often like to go outside when I'm on the phone and the JBLs aren't convenient to use with a stocking cap, so I'd thought briefly about getting something in-ear to wear under my hat. These were $35 and the reviews were good. I liked that the case wirelessly charges the ear buds, and the case can be charged wirelessly too. My Samsung phone has wireless charging so I already have two wireless chargers and they're very convenient (especially given that the USB port on my phone was getting sketchy). So I figured I'd give them a try. I played a variety of my favorite music. I first asked for Jeff Buckley live music and the first song that started playing as I stepped outside was "Hallelujah." I walked around the property listening to my favorite music and before I knew it I had been listening to music for about three hours. I had really only cared about the sound quality for phone calls and whether they would stay in my ears (which is usually a problem for me). They never came close to falling out and they are comfortable. For phone calls the sound quality is very good on both ends. And though they're rated as having a 33' range I walked all around the house and got considerably farther than that from my phone with two walls separating the devices and I had no dropouts. Overall I am so happy with them that after a week of using them I ordered a backup pair.I have three VERY minor niggles but even combined I wouldn't consider them significant enough to knock off even ½ star. First, I had trouble gripping them well enough to get them out of the case quickly when I got an unexpected phone call. I started leaving them on a paper towel on the table next to me, but it now seems I've discovered the right way to grip them. Second, though they have a voice announcement of which side is which when first removed from the case, I was concerned that I might confuse L and R as they don't appear to have any visible indicators. My solution was to use my fine-point permanent marker to write an L on the left one. Third, one of my wireless phone chargers is a tilted stand that holds my phone at a convenient angle. I was unable to get the Ear buds case to wirelessly charge on that one until last night when I accidentally discovered that the problem was that the case was too small to hit the sweet spot on the charger. I solved the problem by boosting the case up with a pad of mini sticky notes (as shown in the photo).EDIT (I apologize if I forget to come back to delete my previous review):None of the above has changed but I forgot to mention that these are NOT good for noise isolation (at least not the way they fit me) but I prefer it that way. I'm a musician and music sounds less natural to me when the surrounding environment is completely eliminated, and I like being able to have a conversation or hear a knock at the door without removing them. Even without a tight seal I never have to reseat them and the sound quality stays consistent (a first for me after trying several other brands).UPDATE: I've been using these ear buds for five weeks now. I use them for hours every day and they continue to impress me. On three occasions only the right channel had a signal when I initially put them in to listen to music, but each time I put them back in the case and took them out again (which turned them off and on) and they worked normally. I've only had this happen with music and only when I first take them out of the case (i.e. it hasn't happened while on a call or after I've been listening to music with both working).

reviews.author: A. W. Straub
reviews.comment: My original Kindle support had been discontinued. It really sucked that they didn't make a mechanism to side load documents so that you could donate it to someone here or abroad. But!!!The new kindle is larger, has easier to use features, charges with a USB-C connection, plays your Audible audio books, has a bluetooth connection, books loaded by wifi, great backlight and easy-on-the-eyes adjustable fonts. reviews.author: Antiochian
reviews.comment: I received my Kindle PW (Paper White) 2024 yesterday!My Kindle History Up to Current:I was using the previous PW which I loved until losing it on a flight - so I dusted off my 2018 PW, popped on a new case and have been using it again for the past 2 years again.Initially I was holding out for the Colorsoft version. However, when it finally came out the reviews were mediocre to poor. The clincher against my buying the Colorsoft was reading that even in B&W mode, the resolution wasn't as crisp as the standard Kindle PW products. So given the choice between mediocre resolution + mediocre color vs excellent B&W I opted for the 2024 PW.From reading reviews on it across the spectrum here, I admit I had the return already prepared.However, my unit arrived in beautiful condition.Color:The chief thing I was looking for was the complaint regarding predominantly yellow screen with the bottom ‘yellower’ band. Not sure if these were faults with the earlier units.On mine, if I have warmth at 0 and the brightness turned up, the color while not being cool, is about as neutral as possible against physical paper. Dimming to 0 relying on ambient light exaggerates the warmth on the Kindle device especially in my place which uses 2700K warm white light sources.The uniformity on the page is perfect - I have not been able to create the darker color band on the lower screen that several reviewers have reported.I haven't yet taken it out into sunlight. I still find the page color at all spectrums is well within my comfort for reading as with paper books where there are also many variations of white color on the pages under different light sources.Resolution:Before ordering I researched the difference between eink and eink carta as my 2018 PW also has 300 ppi. I can't say there is a noticeable difference in the clarity between the 2018 and 2024 unless I look at it under magnifying glass side by side. The difference is nowhere near as detectable as when I upgraded from my 1st gen Kindle to the 2018 PW. In any case both are acceptable and the 2024 resolution is crisp and beautiful as I expected.EDIT: I finally used this at night in the dark with the brightness set at 8.During the day, the resolution to my naked eye looked about the same as my 2018 PW.At night though, the 2024 PW looks far neater and crisper than the older model, even though both are 300 points (the eink Carta difference at work)Performance:This area is where I could really feel the upgrade.I had no complaints on reading the 2018, but starting, inputting my pin or typing anything in the search area, there was noticeable lag that I was accustomed to since using my first Kindle device.The 2024 has almost no latency; if it does I have a hard time noticing it. Whether keying in my PIN or typing a search, it is now as instantly responsive as typing on my phone or tablet.The page turning is as crisp as advertised, and I’m enjoying the animation.Size, Weight, Etc .Form Factor - I'm still in love!Size - I loved the compact size of the 2018 - almost same as small paperback. While the 2024 is a hair larger, I know I'll acclimate with no problem. It's now about the same as a larger paperback - but much lighter in most cases. I also use it with the Cobak Jade color case - while I love the minimalism of the naked Kindle device, having the stand for me is a must rather than having to hold it. Of course, I remove the case when I want to use it in the hot tub.Power Button LocationJury is still out on this.I really wish they'd move the power button to the top. On all the Kindles I have owned over the years, I'm annoyed when I hold the unit (even with the case) my finger tends to brush the power button putting the unit to sleep while I'm reading!On this 2024 PW, I'm noticing that with the increased width and offset position of the button, this may be enough for me to avoid the problem as I typically hold the unit on the bottom dead center, so I'll reserve judgement until I have used the product more.Overall, while I could have used my 2018 a few more years, the improvements in the 2024 made upgrading completely worthwhile.

reviews.author: Eclectic Reader
reviews.comment: Imagine holding a thousand books in your hand. Imagine wearing your jammies while getting that next book in your series, and starting into it a minute later. Imagine reading at night in bed without needing a lamp because your book is backlit (and the light doesn’t hurt your eyes). Imagine having your kindle read to you (even if you don’t have audiobooks) with text to speech while you drive or fold laundry.The 12th edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is a fabulous device and well-worth considering if you read a lot. It’s not too big, not heavy, waterproof, and easy to carry in your purse or backpack. Note that if you get a cover with it (highly recommended), when you open the cover the Kindle turns on automatically to the last page you were reading. With the cover open it feels like you’re holding a thin book -- or fold back the cover if you prefer.The Kindle E-reader is not a computer. It’s not a tablet or a phone. It is a gizmo that acts like a book with a black-and-white flat e-ink screen showing typed sentences and paragraphs. You turn pages one at a time, just like a book. There is no movement on the page and no distraction or advertisement*. It is just text, plus any images that the author has included to illustrate his book.*NOTE: The advertisements on the Kindle are on the main page not the individual book pages and just show books you might like. They are unobtrusive.The backlighting, unlike a computer, tablet, or phone, is gentle because the Kindle’s light is directed onto the screen, not into your eyes. You can change lighting level and add warmth (yellow lighting), decide on dark screen or light screen, and change the size of the print to make your reading experience “just the way you like it.”It’s super-simple to access your own ebooks or to find new ones either on your computer or directly on the Kindle. They load in less than a minute onto the Kindle, ready for reading. Keep in mind if you are a reader that ebooks tend to be half or less the price of the same books in print. You can even find FREE ebooks and audiobooks on Amazon and/or use the Libby app (libbyapp.com) to borrow LOCAL LIBRARY books. You may want to consider subscribing to Kindle Unlimited for $12/month so you can download an even wider selection of free ebooks, audiobooks, and magazines from Amazon to keep as long as you want.Can you tell I love my Kindle? I am wowed by having so many books so easily accessible — not like the time I took that 5-hour flight with one crummy poorly written book and nothing else to do. This 12th generation Kindle is fantastic. The battery lasts a long time. The screen is plenty sensitive for page turns and navigation. I go through one or two books a week easy with this little device.Ebooks have revolutionized the publishing industry, and if you are a reader, the Kindle may be exactly what you’re looking for. If you read many ebooks on your phone or a tablet, consider being kind to your eyes with a Kindle. If you are resisting because you aren’t sure you’ll like ebooks as well as print books, I say what the heck, the Kindle may be worth a try. It’s like driving a racing car rather than a horse and buggy. You might decide you love it.*NOTE: To enable TTS (text to speech) so that your kindle can read to you without audiobooks, turn on your wireless headphones or speaker. Then on your Kindle, tap the top of the screen, then hit the three dots on the right. Go to Settings. Hit Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, then Bluetooth Devices. Select your device so your Kindle will recognize it.Next, close the window and go back to Settings. Hit Accessibility, then turn on Voiceview screen reader. The Kindle should start talking to you. If it’s glitchy, just turn off your bluetooth device then turn it on again. Remember that you have to give double taps not single taps on the Kindle to navigate actions. If you want to change the volume or reading speed (I like 1.25x) just double tap on Voiceview screen to show and customize your settings.

reviews.author: Ashley
reviews.comment: I've had a Kindle Fire for years now and kept buying a new version when the old ones would give out. They seemed to not hold up super well (the Fire) but they are the cheapest Kindle option. Finally decided, since I wasn't really using the tablet feature of the Fire, to go with a Paperwhite instead and the difference has been very noticeable. The Paperwhite is definitely the better quality Kindle - more durable, not nearly as heavy as the Fire, which makes it much easier to carry around or hold for long periods of time. I got a Pop Socket for the back of mine and it's even easier to hold, especially when you've got an infant contact napping on you and only have one hand to use. The readability is great - it doesn't glitch out (so far) like the Fire often does. The backlight is great - I read with it in bed quite often and have no issues seeing the screen. The size is perfect - closer to a traditional paperback and very lightweight. The only issues with functionality would be that it does not support any apps, like Libby, but it's easy enough to download books from Libby using my phone, so that's not a big deal. Overall, I'm very happy with the Paperweight and wish I would have skipped the Fire altogether. For the price, I think the Paperwhite is probably the best option for what it does. The battery life is amazing on the Paperwhite - I usually only have to charge it once every 3-4 weeks with casual reading. The Color Soft option would also be nice, but I don't think it's necessarily worth the price increase, unless having color options is extremely important to you. Overall, a great option for someone just looking for a nice e-reader.

reviews.author: Jane D.
reviews.comment: I have 2 other Insignia TVs that I purchased in 2020. Neither is a FireTV - Just regular TVs and they work great - still. I was looking for a larger TV and I had zero reservations about buying Insignia again. I was hugely surprised that I had an absolute miserable experience to set it up and later, watch. Problem 1: Wouldn’t connect with remote. Contacted Amazon via chat. Was told to unplug TV. Didn’t work. Unplugged again. Didn’t work. Unplugged modem and router. Connected to remote. Problem 2: Wouldn’t play Amazon Prime. Called this time. Spoke to first Amazon rep for over an hour. Got disconnected. Called back. Another hour. The guy couldn't recommend anything other than what the first Amazon guy said which was to disconnect my router and modem, unplug the TV and try again. The TV gets to a screen that says it "needs an update." Click on it to start the update which takes forever and then the TV restarts on its own and returns you back to the original blacked out "apps" that it is supposed to support (you can't see them, but they are supposedly there). Tried several times, and it kept going through the same cycle of "needing an update, waiting for 45 min for the cycle, restarting TV." Problem 3: Amazon phone rep asks for serial number which I read to him from a photograph I took of the back of the TV. He says it’s invalid. What I read to him clearly says "Serial Number" plus it had a manufacture date of June 2025. He asked me to send him the photo as he couldn't validate the serial number. I also gave him my Amazon order number. He said the photo shows another serial number - smaller and way less obvious - with a manufacture date of 1 year earlier (2024!) than the larger, central label with the "invalid serial number." What's going on with that Amazon? Are you slapping on a year younger serial number and manufacture date to make the TV look newer and not like it's one that has been in your store room for over a year? I bought the thing 24 hours ago. Problem 4: There is no user manual. Problem 5: The power cord hole to plug in is hidden with absolutely no reference on any of the 2-page pamphlet where it is located on the back of the TV. Other reviewers have mentioned this. If I didn't read a customer review, I never would have found the power connector. It's vertical! There's an indentation on the left side of the TV as you are facing the back. Hidden at the top of it (it's totally concealed - feel with your finger for it) is the input for the electric cord. Problem 6: Once started - there's still the issue of it going thru different screens with rectangles of the supposed apps it has all blacked out so you can’t see which app it is. No icons. Problem 7: When you finally get it to work and see the apps - and let's say you choose a movie on Amazon Prime - if you put it on "pause" and leave the room to get a snack , the TV will turn itself off. When you turn it back on you won't see the movie, but instead the home screen with all the apps. When you choose "Amazon Prime Video" to get your movie - the thing doesn't even show you the movie at this point. You have to use the search function to find said movie. The only saving grace is that when you find the movie, it does let you resume from where you left off. Other reviewers have noted that there is no setting to avoid the heavy lifting of trying to find your movie again. The auto shut-off engages to "save power" according to the other reviewers. I haven't experienced it shutting off while I'm watching a movie - only when I put it on "pause." As others have said, the interface is super sluggish. reviews.author: Jessica
reviews.comment: These Sound ore by Anker Q20i headphones are absolutely amazing. I wanted noise cancelling headphones to block out the noise of home - I have 3 kids that always have some sort of device and my fiancé who ALWAYS has the tv on and loud. I love that I can pop these on if if I’m not playing anything through them at the moment.- I also love the fact that they can be connected/paired to multiple devices. They are currently paired to my phone, iPad, and switch lite. I use these a lot to play music through my phone or while gaming on my switch lite. BONUS- you can simultaneously have these connected to 2 devices at once. Using them while gaming but also connected to my phone so I won’t miss an important phone call.The headphones do have specific sides R/L that are marked accordingly. If you out them on backwards, they still work BUT if you are trying to use the mic, it will drastically impact the ability for the other person to hear you- so just make sure you put them on the right way.- most headphones are EXTREMELY big on my head as I do have a smaller head- others would fall off the back of my head if I tilted it backwards or fly off the front when I sat up. These do not do that! Do they move some? Yes, but they are by far the best fitting headphones I have ever tried.-also, I have never been able to wear headphones around my neck because they always make me feel like I’m choking, these however don’t and are the first ones I have ever been able to wear around my neck when needing to pause use for a time.- The ear pads/pillows are SO comfortable, they literally feel like little pillow clouds on my ears. They are comfortable enough to lay down with while wearing and I mean laying on my side too.- the sound is incredible, the volume control is top notch! You can turn the volume up all the way if you like, but it’s really not necessary, and I have hearing loss on both sides. (See screenshot showing my perfect volume level with these)- There is an app you can download and adjust your equalizer to personalize it. I just use the Bass booster setting.- the battery life is amazing- far superior to my earbuds. I have only charged them once since I bought them yet and I have had them for nearly 2 weeks now.- these are actually my second pair as the first ones the band seemed as though it had been stretched out and had a pin hole in the ear pad. They replaced them super quick without issue.- they are very durable as previously stated with me sleeping on them. Initially I just tossed them into my bag, but I wanted to protect my investment (I normally don’t really spend money on myself) so I was even able to get a case for these!- oh, I almost forgot! I love how you can fold these too for storage! Makes it super nice for sure!If you’re in doubt, take the jump- I promise you won’t regret your purchase with these!

reviews.author: Chase Purdum
reviews.comment: I've been using the Soundcore by Anker Q20i headphones for a while now, and they've been really impressive. reviews.author: InteractiveLogic
reviews.comment: The title of the review sets the stage and helps to understand where I'm coming from when I purchased the Soundcore by Anker Q20i headphones.BACKSTORYA few years ago I had purchased a pair of Apple AirPods Max, which are probably the best pair of headphones I've ever owned: amazing sound quality, awesome noise cancellation, and unreal support for Transparency Mode. However due to Apple's dubious quality of engineering on that product, they begin to fail after what I consider be too short a time.When they died this last time, I began looking for cheaper alternatives. The obvious one is the Beats Studio Pro, which are actually priced very well for a decent pair of headphones. Instead, I wanted to get something that was a cheaper stopgap, so I started exploring the over-the-ear Soundcore headphones by Anker, because I had had decent experience with them in the past with their Bluetooth earbuds and also approximately 10 years ago I had one of the successor models to the Q20i. So I thought I would give it a shot.I purchased a different pair of Soundcore headphones at first, but when they arrived they had an offensive smell and had to send them back. After that experience, I do not know what motivated me to try the Soundcore Q20i model, but immediately on arrival I had a different experience. There was no offensive smell, the headphones are very comfortable on my (admittedly large) head.SOUND QUALITYAs far as sound quality is concerned, they are passable-to-pretty-good. They initially sounded a little "tinny", but I typically run them with the bass boost and I think I've gotten used to the way that they sound at this point. My typical use case is wearing my headphones pretty much all day listening to droning ambient electronic music so I can focus while working.Therefore, I am not necessarily looking for stellar audio quality, but these are actually pretty good for the price. One cannot compare them to the AirPods Max, because those headphones just blew me away by their quality. But given that this is a $45 pair of headphones, the sound is great—for the price.(I will keep saying that just to keep perspective: "For the price…")TRANSPARENCY MODEThe other reason why I went for these is because I needed a pair of headphones that had Transparency Mode, but I didn't have the extra cash to spend on the Beats Studio Pro. The Q20i surprised me because it has a Transparency Mode in a $45 pair of headphones. It's important to acknowledge that Transparency Mode on the Q20i is *nowhere near* the same experience of Transparency Mode on AirPods Max or AirPods Pro, so don't expect that level. However, it does let in enough ambient sound to allow me to hear sound around me and to have a conversation with someone without having to take the headphones off. That was the crucial feature requirement. So again, for the price, having Transparency Mode at all is pretty amazing.STAR REMOVALThe only reason I took off a star is because I feel that the headphones should have the capacity to remember that I always want to have transparency on, or at least remember the last setting of that mode so that when I turned them on the next time, it will be in the same mode that I left it. These do not do that, and for that, I docked a star.OTHER TOPICSBattery life has been good, but I work at a desk and I can charge them whenever I need to, so I am probably not the best judge of that.The headphones are light and comfortable, and they are very adjustable so they should be able to fit and be comfortable for most wearers. They also fold for easy transportation and seem like a pretty durable construction.CONCLUSIONFor a sub $50 pair of headphones that has transparency mode, has reasonably good sound quality, and so far has been behaving decently on the Bluetooth side connected to a MacBook Pro, I definitely recommend them to someone who is on a tight budget, or someone who just wants a "burner" set of Bluetooth over the ear headphones.

I needed something to use with my Android TV device for watching movies late at night.The sound quality is good, the buttons have indentations and features you can feel with your fingers as needed - though I don't fiddle with the controls much since I use my TV remote to adjust volume, pause etc.I have used these to talk on the phone once and the person on the other end could hear me adequately. I really appreciate the fast sync up time after turning on the headphones to whatever you'll be using them with.As some have mentioned, its a little difficult to tell when the headphones are on or have turned on after holding the power button for a second. Anker is a solid name in portable battery packs but apparently they make other high quality products as well. I can attest to that.
